grade.first_issue: In Step 3, the claim that for every n one can choose m∈N with |(z1+nc1)−(z2+mc2)|<c2 is false: the second progression may initially lie entirely above the first point. For example, for the admissible f(t)=t+1, take z1=2, z2=101 and n=1. This is the approximation step supporting constancy of g, so Rule C applies. It becomes correct by replacing “for any n” with “for all sufficiently large n,” after which a nearest-integer choice of m works.
grade.summary: The stated classification f(x)=x+c, c≥0, is correct. The orbit argument, nonnegativity of g, exclusion of mixed defect levels via connectedness, and final verification are otherwise sound. However, the proof contains a false load-bearing quantifier in its central constancy argument. Although the repair is immediate and preserves the strategy, Rule C caps the score at 5.
strengths: Correctly derives f(f(y))+y=2f(y) and hence invariance of g along forward orbits.
Correctly obtains f^n(y)=y+ng(y) and uses positivity to prove g≥0.
The clopen-set argument excluding coexistence of defects 0 and c is valid.
The converse verification for f(x)=x+c is algebraically correct.

errors.description: The lattice-approximation assertion is false for arbitrary n because m is required to be nonnegative. Only the sufficiently large n version is true. This step is load-bearing for proving that all positive values of g coincide, though it is repaired simply by restricting to sufficiently large n.
